The genus '''''Carthamus''''', the '''[[distaff]] [[thistle]]s''', includes plants in the family [[Asteraceae]].<ref>[https://www.biodiversitylibrary.org/page/358851#page/272/mode/1up Linnaeus, Carl von. 1753.  Species Plantarum 2: 830-831] in Latin</ref> The group is native to Europe, North Africa, and parts of Asia.<ref name=b/><ref>[http://luirig.altervista.org/flora/taxa/floraspecie.php?genere=Carthamus Altervista Flora Italiana, genere Carthamus] includes photos and European distribution maps for 9 species</ref> The flower has been used since ancient times in the Philippines, which it has been called ''kasubha'' by the [[Tagalog people]].<ref>{{Cite book | url=https://books.google.com/books?id=Ca5XDwAAQBAJ&q=Lakan+Balingasay&pg=PA387 |title = Ancient Beliefs and Customs of the Tagalogs|isbn = 9780244348731|date = 2019-05-25| publisher=Lulu.com }}</ref>

The best known species is the [[safflower]] ''([[Carthamus tinctorius]]).''
